_note: Hand-curated registry of VERIFIED Cambridge International facts - qualifications, editions, stage alignment AND the content-use policy. This is the single source of truth that build_cambridge_tree.py materialises into the tree, and the only file where a Cambridge fact may be introduced by hand. Every entry carries source_urls and a verification status. audit_tree.py enforces that nothing claims 'corroborated' without >= 2 source_urls and that no URL appears without a url_status.
_verification_method: Cambridge hosts (cambridgeinternational.org, cambridge.org, help.cambridgeinternational.org) are blocked by this build environment's egress policy (proxy CONNECT 403, checked 2026-08-04), and no page fetch of any host succeeded, so EVERY fact below was established from search-indexed copies of Cambridge's own pages - titles, indexed URLs and snippet extracts - not by first-hand fetch. Quoted wording is snippet-reconstructed and must be re-pulled from the live page before being relied on in a legal context. URLs are recorded ONLY where the URL itself appeared in a search result with its subject attribution; URLs that would merely follow an observed naming pattern are left null. Run scripts/fetch_cambridge_sources.py from a network-enabled machine to confirm everything first-hand.

landing_page.status: Pattern confirmed against many observed landing pages, but DELIBERATELY not used to construct URLs that were not themselves observed - a plausible-but-wrong URL is worse than a null.

documents.legacy_short_form: {code}_y{startYY}-{endYY}_sy.pdf - the machine-friendly identifier used by mirrors and historically by Cambridge
documents.status: The 6-digit document id is opaque and NOT derivable from the syllabus code, so every document URL must be harvested from the subject's own page. Recorded below only where observed with attribution.

_open_questions.question: What do cambridgeinternational.org/robots.txt and its sitemap say, and do they carry AI-crawler directives (GPTBot, ClaudeBot, CCBot, Google-Extended)?
_open_questions.status: UNVERIFIED - the single largest evidentiary gap. Targeted searches returned nothing describing the file. Cambridge's corporate posture on AI is restrictive (opt-in author licensing for generative-AI training; opposition to a copyright exception with opt-out), but inferring robots directives from press statements would be a guess.
_open_questions.resolve_with: scripts/fetch_cambridge_sources.py probe reads robots.txt first-hand. Do this BEFORE any bulk fetching.

_open_questions.question: Does cambridge.org/legal/copyright, including its text-and-data-mining clause, govern cambridgeinternational.org, or does Cambridge International's own /privacy-and-legal/terms-and-conditions/ diverge?
_open_questions.status: UNVERIFIED - the copyright page scopes itself to 'Cambridge.org website pages'. Cambridge International maintains a separate terms page that could not be read.
_open_questions.resolve_with: Read https://www.cambridgeinternational.org/privacy-and-legal/terms-and-conditions/ first-hand and reconcile it against RIGHTS.json.

_open_questions.question: How many examination series does the PUBLIC subject past-papers page retain?
_open_questions.status: UNVERIFIED - a five-year limit is documented for the School Support Hub specifically, driven partly by third-party permissions being cleared for five years. Whether the same window governs the public pages is plausible but unstated.
_open_questions.resolve_with: Observe a subject past-papers page directly.

_open_questions.question: Is the policy wording recorded in content_use recorded verbatim?
_open_questions.status: UNVERIFIED - all of it is snippet-reconstructed, and sentence subjects drift between 'Cambridge' and 'we' across renderings. The SUBSTANCE of each rule was corroborated across three or four independent searches; the exact wording was not, so nothing here is presented as a quotation.
_open_questions.resolve_with: Re-pull each passage from the live help-centre article before quoting it anywhere that matters.

content_use.rights_holder: Cambridge University Press & Assessment / Cambridge Assessment International Education (UCLES)
content_use.headline: Access is open; reproduction is not. Cambridge publishes question papers, mark schemes, examiner reports and specimen materials openly on its own website, so obtaining them is easy - and separately, explicitly, refuses permission for electronic publication of that material in any format. Do not read the ease of access as permission.

past_papers.public_access_detail: Question papers, mark schemes, examiner reports and specimen materials are published as open PDFs under cambridgeinternational.org/Images/ and linked from each subject's own past-papers page. No login is required. This CORRECTS an assumption made earlier while building this tree, that Cambridge papers were login-gated: they are not, and the distinction matters because the real constraint is rights, not access.
past_papers.school_support_hub: A login-gated superset for registered Cambridge schools - teacher accounts are created by the school's Support Hub coordinator, and access is explicitly not open to individuals or third-party organisations. It adds schemes of work, community resources and coordinator tooling. Materials older than about five years are withdrawn from it, partly because third-party copyright permissions inside papers are cleared for five years only.
past_papers.use_in_classroom_detail: Cambridge permits teachers AT CAMBRIDGE SCHOOLS to download and print past papers for use with their own students. That is a print-and-use permission, not a re-hosting one; it does not extend to non-Cambridge schools, tutors, individuals or third-party organisations, and the same source states the materials cannot be used for publication or resale without prior approval.
past_papers.rule: Cambridge does not grant permission for the use of complete examination papers, nor for electronic publication in any format of questions from past examination papers, nor for the reproduction of mark schemes, examiners' reports or questions set in multiple-choice form. Its refusal to permit publication on any website or school intranet is stated categorically - note that this reaches a school's OWN intranet, so there is no internal-network carve-out. The stated reason is loss of control over material once it is online, including incidents of Cambridge material being sold online.
past_papers.commercial_or_not: The prohibition is not conditioned on commercial use: non-commercial electronic republication is refused on the same terms. This is stricter than the IEB position recorded in ../IEB/SOURCES.md, where the restriction is on commercial gain and personal study use is permitted.
past_papers.permission_route: A written application - a .docx form requiring a hand-written signature and photocopies of the material - is the only documented route, answered within about three weeks of a complete form. Note that the same document describing the process also states the blanket refusal above, so the process itself cannot grant electronic publication of paper questions. No paid or commercial licensing tier was found; treat that as absence of evidence rather than evidence of absence.
past_papers.gate_rationale: Cambridge states it does not grant permission for electronic publication, in any format, of past-paper questions, mark schemes, examiners' reports or multiple-choice questions, and refuses publication on any website or intranet. The refusal is not conditioned on commercial use, so no reading of our use clears it. Only a written permission grant can, and the same document that describes the permission process states the blanket refusal - so assume refusal until a grant exists on file.

mark_schemes_examiner_reports.rule: Named explicitly alongside past-paper questions in Cambridge's refusal of electronic publication, notwithstanding that Cambridge publishes them openly itself.
mark_schemes_examiner_reports.gate_rationale: Cambridge states it does not grant permission for electronic publication, in any format, of past-paper questions, mark schemes, examiners' reports or multiple-choice questions, and refuses publication on any website or intranet. The refusal is not conditioned on commercial use, so no reading of our use clears it. Only a written permission grant can, and the same document that describes the permission process states the blanket refusal - so assume refusal until a grant exists on file.

syllabuses.access_route: Published openly on cambridgeinternational.org, no login.
syllabuses.rule: Cambridge syllabus PDFs carry their own copyright block granting REGISTERED CENTRES permission to copy material from the booklet for their own INTERNAL use, with third-party-acknowledged material excluded even internally. That is an affirmative grant on the face of the document, and it is materially more permissive than the past-paper position, which carries no such grant and is expressly refused for electronic publication.
syllabuses.do_not_over_read: The grant runs to registered centres for internal use. No statement was found granting general redistribution, mirroring or re-hosting of syllabus PDFs, and no Cambridge International document was found under any open licence. Whether 'copy for internal use' extends to electronic internal distribution such as a VLE is genuinely unresolved: the wording is medium-neutral, but the adjacent third-party carve-out says 'photocopy', which arguably implies print.
syllabuses.practical_reading: Ingesting a public syllabus to derive structure - topic lists, assessment structure, learning objectives - for internal curriculum mapping is the intended use of a published syllabus, and is the basis on which this tree proceeds. Reproducing substantial syllabus prose verbatim in a shipped product is a separate question needing its own permission check.
syllabuses.gate_rationale: Cambridge grants registered centres permission to copy syllabus material for their own internal use. A commercial product built by a third party is not a registered centre using material internally, so the grant does not plainly reach this repository's shipping use. That is the licence not clearly covering our case - an owner decision - rather than a prohibition. Ingesting the public syllabus to derive structure for internal curriculum mapping sits inside the ordinary purpose of a published syllabus and is what this tree does.

specimen_materials.gate_rationale: Specimen papers and specimen mark schemes are assessment materials of the same kind as live past papers, published by Cambridge alongside them. Cambridge's refusal names 'questions from past examination papers' and mark schemes; whether specimen material is read as inside that phrase was NOT established. Gated conservatively at the same level as past papers, because the conservative reading is the safe one and loosening a gate requires first-hand evidence, never an assumption.

text_and_data_mining.summary: Cambridge's copyright page carries an explicit text-and-data-mining clause: non-commercial TDM over content to which you have LAWFUL ACCESS is permitted, subject to linking to the underlying content, with local copies deleted when the non-commercial project ends and results publishable only where no Cambridge content is made available commercially. Cambridge expressly reserves its rights and opts OUT of granting commercial TDM rights.
text_and_data_mining.consequence: Directly material to any AI or education product built on this tree. A commercial product derived from mined Cambridge content sits outside the granted permission. The non-commercial permission is also conditioned on lawful access - satisfied for the public syllabus PDFs, not satisfied for anything obtained from an unauthorised mirror.
text_and_data_mining.scope_caveat: The clause sits on cambridge.org and scopes itself to 'Cambridge.org website pages'. Whether it governs cambridgeinternational.org is an open question - see _open_questions.cie_site_terms_scope.
text_and_data_mining.ai_use: Cambridge expressly reserves commercial text-and-data-mining rights and opts out of granting them, permitting non-commercial TDM only, over content to which you have lawful access, with local copies deleted at project end. Its parent has separately adopted an OPT-IN posture for licensing author content to generative-AI companies and has publicly opposed a copyright exception with opt-out. This repository is a pipeline that feeds curriculum material to a model, so this clause is not a footnote - it is arguably the most product-relevant rule here, and it points the same way as the College Board's explicit anti-AI clause recorded in ../US/RIGHTS.json: a generic reproduction permission would not cover AI use. Any permission sought from Cambridge should name the AI use explicitly.

third_party_material_inside_papers.finding: Published Cambridge past papers are already PARTIALLY REDACTED documents. Where Cambridge could not clear third-party copyright - poems, prose passages - the material is removed from the published paper, with only the first and last lines plus a reference printed, and acknowledgements published separately in per-series Copyright Acknowledgement Booklets. Third-party permissions are typically cleared for five years, which is part of why older materials are withdrawn.
third_party_material_inside_papers.consequence: A 'complete' paper obtained from an aggregator - one that still contains the unredacted passage - is by construction carrying material Cambridge itself could not license. Using such a copy creates infringement exposure against the third-party rights holder that is separate from, and additional to, Cambridge's own copyright.

aggregators.rule: All third-party redistributors of Cambridge material are excluded as sources. None claims Cambridge authorisation; at least two affirmatively disclaim any affiliation; and the licence such a site would need is one Cambridge's own permissions policy says it does not issue. Cambridge cites misuse of its material online, including resale, as its reason for refusing web publication. Since Cambridge publishes the same documents itself, there is no scenario in which an aggregator is the correct source.
aggregators.note: Aggregators also re-scrape each other - papers served by one carrying another's watermark were observed during research - so provenance through them is unreliable even setting rights aside.

prohibited_in_this_tree.rule: No file in the CAMBRIDGE tree may contain past-paper question text, mark-scheme or memo answers, or examiner-report text, and no URL in it may point at an unauthorised redistributor. audit_tree.py enforces this mechanically so the prohibition survives edits by people who never read the policy.

gate_levels.none: No rights gate. Use freely within the recorded licence.
gate_levels.attribution_required: Reuse is licensed, but a specific notice/citation MUST accompany any publication or public display.
gate_levels.owner_decision_required: The licence does not clearly cover this repository's intended use (for-profit / commercial product). Indexing and internal analysis are fine; an owner decision is required before the content ships to students.
gate_levels.blocked_pending_written_permission: Reproduction requires express written permission from the rights holder. Nothing beyond facts, links and metadata may be ingested.

content_use._gate_vocabulary_note: Deliberately identical to the gate_levels in lessons/curriculum/US/RIGHTS.json. The unit differs: the US tree gates whole FRAMEWORKS because each has its own rights holder, whereas Cambridge is a single rights holder whose gate differs by DOCUMENT CLASS - syllabuses and assessment materials are governed by different permissions. Same vocabulary, different key, so cross-tree tooling still reads both.
summary_for_owner: SYLLABUSES (the content layer this tree is built on): public, and ingesting them to derive curriculum structure is ordinary use. Gate is owner_decision_required only for SHIPPING substantial syllabus prose in a commercial product - not for the mapping work itself.

PAST PAPERS, MARK SCHEMES, EXAMINER REPORTS: blocked. Openly downloadable, but electronic reproduction is refused outright, commercial or not. The CAPS/DBE worked-example pipeline therefore has NO Cambridge equivalent and must not be pointed at Cambridge material.

AI/TDM: commercial text-and-data-mining rights are expressly reserved. If permission is ever sought, it must name the generative-AI use specifically - a reproduction permission alone would not cover what this repository does.
Stricter than the IEB (which bars reproduction for commercial gain but permits personal study use) and in the same bracket as the College Board's AP/SAT gate in the US tree.

_exam_series.note: Stated for AS & A Level on the observed subject-list page. Whether all three series apply to every IGCSE subject here is NOT established - confirm per subject from the official syllabus before any scheduler relies on it.

_edition_model.summary: A Cambridge syllabus is published for a named set of examination years - 'for examination in June and November 2025, 2026 and 2027' - with point versions inside a cycle plus separate syllabus-update documents.
_edition_model.critical: Versioning is PER SYLLABUS CODE, not global. The nominal cycle is three years, but observed cycles run one, two and three years and are staggered across subjects, so a single 'current Cambridge edition' field would be wrong. Always key an edition to the pair (syllabus_code, exam_year_range).

_grading_sets.finding: Many IGCSE subjects exist as TWO syllabus codes with identical content and assessment, differing only in the reported grade set (A*-G versus 9-1). A school chooses one at entry and cannot switch after the entries deadline.
_grading_sets.unverified: The 9-1 codes for Chemistry, Physics, Economics and Accounting were NOT established. A guessed numbering pattern was tested during research and proved wrong, so none is recorded. Do not invent them.
_grading_sets.repo_decision: This registry keys each subject on the A*-G code, the one corroborated for every subject here. If a Cambridge stream ever serves a 9-1 school, model the pair explicitly rather than substituting a code.

stage_alignment.problem: Cambridge is a global curriculum author using its own stages (Cambridge Primary, Cambridge Lower Secondary, Cambridge Upper Secondary = IGCSE/O Level, Cambridge Advanced = AS & A Level), not national grade numbers. This repository's tree contract is grade10/grade11/grade12, the South African FET phase used by the CAPS and IEB trees.
stage_alignment.cambridge_disclaims_a_mapping: Cambridge states that its age ranges are for guidance only, that there are no formal age regulations for IGCSE entry, and that centres set their own entry policy; IGCSE runs one year rather than two in some countries. Cambridge assigns internal stage numbers only to Primary and Lower Secondary (Stages 1-9) - Upper Secondary and Advanced are identified by qualification, not year. So there is no authoritative Cambridge grade table to follow, by design.
stage_alignment.convention: REPOSITORY CONVENTION, not a Cambridge statement. Every syllabus file repeats this caveat.
stage_alignment.basis: Cambridge's own 14-16 age band for Upper Secondary against South African Grade 10 (about 15) and Grade 11 (about 16), plus the one point on which every South African third-party source agrees: AS Level sits at Grade 12. Those sources disagree with each other about IGCSE placement - Grade 10, Grade 11, or spanning both - which is itself evidence that no single mapping is authoritative.

grade11.note: IGCSE examination normally sat at the end of this year.

alternative_pathways.description: IGCSE taught across Grades 9-10, AS in Grade 11, A Level (A2) in Grade 12. Common where a school starts Cambridge earlier.
IGCSE completed in one year, which Cambridge states happens in some countries. Collapses the grade10/grade11 span of the default pathway.
alternative_pathways.note: Recorded because Cambridge documents it, not because it is common in the South African schools this repo currently serves.

stage_alignment.unresolved: A full Cambridge International A Level is a two-year course of which AS is year one, so a school on the default pathway completes A2 in a thirteenth year, which has no grade12-keyed slot in this contract. A Level must NOT be silently folded into grade12. Any product serving Cambridge A Level students has to decide how to represent that year; this tree does not invent one.

stages.name: Cambridge Advanced
stages.typical_course_length_years: AS 1 year; full A Level 2 years

maths.equivalence_note: Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics and AS & A Level Mathematics correspond directly to this repository's academic 'maths' subject. Two structural differences from CAPS have no analogue and must not be flattened away: the IGCSE Core/Extended tier split, with different papers and capped grade ranges, and the AS/A Level component-choice model, where a candidate's papers depend on which applied components the school enters.

qualifications.title: Mathematics
research_notes: TRAP for the curation pass: 0580 was RESTRUCTURED for first examination June 2025. Research found consistent secondary reports that each paper is now 50% of the total, with one non-calculator and one calculator paper per tier (Core = Papers 1 and 3, Extended = Papers 2 and 4). It also found revision sites still publishing the PRE-2025 figures - Extended Paper 2 at 70 marks and 35%, Paper 4 at 130 marks and 65% - as if current. Take the structure from the fetched syllabus, and version-gate anything derived from papers sat before 2025.
Grade ranges appear to differ between subjects: Extended was reported as A*-E for 0580 but A*-G for some sciences. Do not generalise one tier-to-grade rule across subjects; read each syllabus.

qualifications.title: Mathematics
research_notes: 9709 is assembled from named components - Pure Mathematics 1 to 3, Mechanics, Probability & Statistics 1 and 2 - rather than a fixed paper set: AS is Paper 1 plus one applied component, and the full A Level adds Paper 3 plus two applied components, with at least one combination reported as not permitted. Secondary sources agreed on this shape, but it is single-source-grade evidence. Take the permitted combinations from the syllabus itself: getting them wrong would mis-scope an entire stream.

adjacent_not_mapped.title: Cambridge IGCSE International Mathematics
adjacent_not_mapped.why_not_mapped: A distinct IGCSE maths syllabus - tiered Core/Extended like 0580, but requiring a graphic display calculator and adding investigation and modelling papers. A legitimate alternative for a Cambridge stream, but a different qualification, so not the default mapping.

adjacent_not_mapped.title: Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics - Additional
adjacent_not_mapped.why_not_mapped: A separate advanced IGCSE subject carrying calculus, taken alongside rather than instead of 0580. Recorded because a Cambridge stream serving strong candidates may need it. Its 2025-2027 edition removed indices and surds as assumed knowledge, added coordinate geometry of the circle and introduced a non-calculator paper.

adjacent_not_mapped.title: Cambridge O Level Mathematics (Syllabus D)
adjacent_not_mapped.why_not_mapped: The O Level route rather than IGCSE, offered where a centre runs O Level. The same reasoning applies to O Level Additional Mathematics 4037.

adjacent_not_mapped.title: Cambridge International AS & A Level Mathematics - Further
adjacent_not_mapped.why_not_mapped: A separate advanced qualification for candidates already taking 9709. Structure not researched.

mathematical_literacy.equivalence_note: Mathematical Literacy is a South-Africa-specific NSC subject - numeracy applied to real-life contexts, taken INSTEAD of academic Mathematics. Cambridge International publishes no equivalent. Its entire Upper Secondary maths suite (0580, 0980, 0607, 0606, 0444, 4024, 4037) is academic mathematics; the Core tiers of 0580 and 0607 are grade-capped tiers of the same academic syllabus rather than a different subject in kind; and Functional Skills Mathematics, the UK numeracy-in-context qualification, is not a Cambridge International product. This folder exists so that tooling walking curriculum/{CAPS,IEB,CAMBRIDGE}/{subject} finds a uniform layout, and it records the absence explicitly rather than silently omitting the subject or forcing a false match.

adjacent_not_mapped.title: Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics (Core tier)
adjacent_not_mapped.why_not_mapped: A grade-capped tier of academic mathematics sharing content with Extended - a difficulty tier, not a subject of a different kind.

adjacent_not_mapped.title: Cambridge IGCSE International Mathematics (Core tier)
adjacent_not_mapped.why_not_mapped: Closest in spirit, since it adds modelling and real-life contexts, but still a full academic maths syllabus that feeds AS Level, and itself tiered.

mathematical_literacy.consumer_rule: A Cambridge stream must NOT serve Mathematical Literacy by falling back to the CAPS or IEB tree, and must not substitute 0580 Core or 0607 Core: those are academic mathematics, and the substitution would misrepresent both qualifications to the student. Serve academic Mathematics, or serve nothing and say why.

physical_sciences.equivalence_note: South Africa's 'Physical Sciences' is a single subject combining Physics and Chemistry with no Biology. Cambridge HAS carried exactly that combination - IGCSE Physical Science 0652, whose content is Chemistry sections plus Physics sections and nothing else - but it is being WITHDRAWN, with November 2026 as its final examination series. After that, no single Cambridge qualification matches the South African combination: the multi-science awards (0653 Combined, 0654 Co-ordinated Double) all include Biology, and at AS & A Level there is no combined science option at all. The primary mapping is therefore the Physics + Chemistry PAIR taken as two separate subjects - the only mapping that survives the withdrawal and the only one available at Advanced level.

syllabus_documents.edition_note: Recorded for traceability only - this cycle has ended. A 2026-2028 cycle was indicated during research but not confirmed; find the live edition from the landing page before ingesting.

qualifications.title: Chemistry
research_notes: No paper, mark, duration or weighting figure for 0620 was corroborated at any point during research. Do not assume it mirrors 0625's structure - read the syllabus.

adjacent_not_mapped.title: Cambridge IGCSE Physical Science
adjacent_not_mapped.why_not_mapped: STRUCTURALLY THE EXACT MATCH for South African Physical Sciences - Chemistry sections plus Physics sections, both compulsory, no Biology - but WITHDRAWN, with November 2026 the final examination series. Cambridge names 0610, 0620, 0625, 0653 and 0654 as the alternatives. Not mapped, because a stream built on it would expire immediately; recorded prominently, because anyone comparing the two curricula will find it and needs to know why it is not the answer.

adjacent_not_mapped.title: Cambridge IGCSE Sciences - Co-ordinated (Double Award)
adjacent_not_mapped.why_not_mapped: Biology, Chemistry AND Physics in one cross-referenced syllabus, awarded as two identical grades. Broader than South African Physical Sciences because of the Biology component; mapping it would misstate scope.

adjacent_not_mapped.title: Cambridge IGCSE Science - Combined
adjacent_not_mapped.why_not_mapped: The same three sciences as 0654 but a single award, one grade, and reduced depth. Same Biology objection.

adjacent_not_mapped.title: Cambridge O Level Physics 5054 / Chemistry 5070
adjacent_not_mapped.why_not_mapped: The O Level route rather than IGCSE. No chemistry-plus-physics-only O Level equivalent of 0652 was found; it may not exist.

physical_sciences.consumer_rule: Serving 'physical_sciences' to a Cambridge learner means serving TWO Cambridge subjects. A consumer must resolve which of the pair a topic belongs to, must not present a Combined or Co-ordinated Science scope as if it were the pair, and must not offer 0652 to anyone examined after November 2026.

geography.equivalence_note: Direct subject-name correspondence. Content scope still differs from CAPS - Cambridge Geography has its own themes and its own skills and fieldwork components, including a coursework-or-written-alternative choice that CAPS does not have. The difference must come from the ingested syllabus, never from assumption.

syllabus_documents.edition_note: The forthcoming cycle. Ingest alongside the current one so a stream can be pinned to a student's examination year.

research_notes: No paper count, duration, mark total or weighting was corroborated for 9696. The code is solid; the structure is entirely unestablished.

accounting.equivalence_note: Direct subject-name correspondence, but a real content difference: Cambridge Accounting uses international terminology and IAS-style statement formats where CAPS uses South African conventions. Terminology mapping is a curation task, not a rename.

qualifications.title: Accounting

research_notes: CONFLICT to resolve on fetch: research surfaced two incompatible descriptions of 0452's assessment - one giving Paper 1 as multiple choice at 35 marks and 30% with Paper 2 structured written at 100 marks and 70%, another giving both papers at 120 marks. Neither could be tied confidently to the current single-year 2026 edition. Take the structure only from the fetched syllabus.

adjacent_not_mapped.why_not_mapped: The O Level route rather than IGCSE.

economics.equivalence_note: Direct subject-name correspondence. A new Cambridge IGCSE and O Level Economics 0455 syllabus began teaching in the 2025-26 academic year, so edition selection matters more than usual here.

qualifications.title: Economics

qualifications.title: Economics
research_notes: Reported shape: AS is Papers 1 and 2, the full A Level adds Papers 3 and 4, with multiple-choice papers at both levels and essay sections in Paper 2. Single-source-grade evidence - confirm against the syllabus.
